records.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. We observed a significantly greater reduction in mean total HAM-A score during chamomile versus placebo therapy.
Randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial. A statistically significant change was reported in sleep quality for valerian compared with placebo.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Saw palmetto led to a statistically significant improvement in urinary symptoms compared with placebo.
Randomized controlled trial. Illness duration and severity were not statistically significant with echinacea compared with placebo.
Randomized controlled trial. Black cohosh did not significantly reduce the frequency of vasomotor symptoms compared with placebo.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. There were no statistically significant differences between valerian and placebo on measures of sleep latency or sleep quality.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial. In this study, St John's wort was not effective for treatment of major depression.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial. Ginkgo biloba was not effective in reducing the incidence of dementia or Alzheimer disease.
Double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial. This study fails to support the efficacy of Hypericum perforatum in moderately severe major depression.
Randomized controlled trial. Chamomile significantly reduced GAD symptoms, but did not significantly reduce the rate of relapse.
Randomized trial. The primary sleep-quality difference was not statistically significant, while significantly more valerian participants rated sleep better or much better.
Meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials. Subjective results suggested benefit, although effectiveness was not demonstrated with quantitative or objective measurements.
Echinaforce and its concentrated preparation were significantly more effective than the special Echinacea extract or placebo.
Echinacea reduced the total number of cold episodes, cumulated episode days within the group, and pain-killer medicated episodes.
There was a significant difference between the two groups in terms of severity and number of hot flashes in weeks 4 and 8.
Ginkgo biloba extract given 3 times daily for 12 weeks is no more effective than placebo in treating tinnitus.
Saw palmetto extract was no more effective than placebo for any secondary outcome.
Valerian produced nonsignificant reductions in sleep latency, while physical quality of life was significantly more improved than placebo at 28 days.
Unadjusted analyses showed no protection against progression or memory decline, while adherence-adjusted secondary analyses showed a protective effect.
Black cohosh was not significantly more efficacious than placebo against most menopausal symptoms, including number and intensity of hot flashes.
Neither the improvements nor the global satisfaction were significantly different between the two groups.
Treatment with ginkgo 120 mg twice a day did not improve cognitive performance in persons with MS.
Ginkgo provides no measurable benefit in memory or related cognitive function to adults with healthy cognitive function.
The valerian-hops combination beat placebo on sleep latency, whereas the single valerian extract did not.
